rv.q: Odd is not the word for this couple. How could an adjective suggesting strangeness or surprise apply to a production so calculatedly devoted to the known, the cozy, the conventional? Consider the basic ingredients of the bland, mechanical new revival of Neil Simon’s "Odd Couple," starring Nathan Lane and Matthew Broderick, at the Theater: a play...
Mr. Lane and Mr. Broderick are both gifted comic actors, but they're playing against type here, and the results are mixed at best.
As this set-to-a-metronome production, directed by Joe Mantello, demonstrates with such clarity, the comic languages of "The Producers" and "The Odd Couple" are not the same.

Everything that was originally oh-so-right about the set-up — a divorced man and a divorcing man share digs and ultimately begin replicating the dynamic of their marriages — is still hilariously right.

cn.t: This revival of Neil Simon's classic comedy receives mixed reviews, with critics praising the play itself but finding the production bland and mechanical, while Lane and Broderick are seen as playing against type with uneven results.
